entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Iván Castro is a former United States Army officer who continued serving on active duty in the Special Forces despite losing his eyesight. He was one of three blind active duty officers who served in the U.S. Army and the only blind officer serving in the United States Army Special Forces. Castro served at the Special Operations Recruiting Battalion as the Assistant Operations Officer/Total Army Involvement Recruiting Coordinator before his retirement in 2017. He is an advocate of rehabilitation, employment and education for those wounded in combat and participates in various races and marathons as a contestant.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Iván Castro's determination to serve in the Special Forces despite losing his eyesight has inspired others with disabilities and contributed to increased awareness about rehabilitation and employment opportunities for wounded veterans. His story serves as a testament to the resilience of individuals affected by combat injuries.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Iván Castro's determination to continue serving in the Special Forces despite losing his eyesight has inspired others with visual impairments to pursue careers in the military and special operations. His advocacy for rehabilitation, employment, and education for wounded veterans has had a regional impact on the U.S. military's approach to supporting service members with disabilities.
